43263-the-arrow-of-fire-a-mystery-story-.title: The Arrow Of Fire
43263-the-arrow-of-fire-a-mystery-story-.creator: Roy J. Snell
43263-the-arrow-of-fire-a-mystery-story-.description: A book by Roy J. Snell. In his three years of wandering Johnny had known mystery, romance, and adventure aplenty. He had glided up dark mangrove-bordered streams at the heart of tropical America. He had crept into dungeons in the haunted castle of Haiti. He had felt the call of the barren tundras and smoking mountains of British Columbia and Alaska.

arxiv-1502-07516.title: Nijenhuis Integrability for Killing Tensors This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Analytical Mechanics and Differential Geometry in honour of Sergio Benenti. The full collection is available at http://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Benenti.html
arxiv-1502-07516.creator: Konrad SCHÖBEL
arxiv-1502-07516.description: Abstract The fundamental tool in the classification of orthogonal coordinate systems in which the Hamilton–Jacobi and other prominent equations can be solved by a separation of variables are second order Killing tensors which satisfy the Nijenhuis integrability conditions. The latter are a system of three non-linear partial differential equations.

arxiv-2006-04092.title: The Measure Preserving Isometry Groups of Metric Measure Spaces This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Scalar and Ricci Curvature in honor of Misha Gromov on his 75th Birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Gromov.html
arxiv-2006-04092.creator: Yifan GUO †‡
arxiv-2006-04092.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yifan GUO †‡. Bochner’s theorem says that if M M is a compact Riemannian manifold with negative Ricci curvature, then the isometry group Iso ⁡ ( M ) \operatorname{Iso}(M) is finite. In this article, we show that if ( X , d , m ) (X,d,m) is a compact metric measure space with synthetic negative Ricci curvature in Sturm’s sense, then the measure preserving isometry group Iso ⁡ ( X , d , m ) \operatorname{Iso}(X,d,m) is finite.

arxiv-2206-02180.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Mars Imagery Classification and Segmentation Journal: JACM Volume: 37 4 0 8 CCS: Computing methodologies Semi-supervised learning settings CCS: Computing methodologies Object recognition CCS: Computing methodologies Image segmentation
arxiv-2206-02180.creator: Wenjing Wang, Lilang Lin, Zejia Fan, Jiaying Liu
arxiv-2206-02180.description: Abstract . With the progress of Mars exploration, numerous Mars image data are collected and need to be analyzed. However, due to the severe train-test gap and quality distortion of Martian data, the performance of existing computer vision models is unsatisfactory.

arxiv-2211-16732.title: Determining Dust Properties in Protoplanetary Disks: SED-derived Masses and Settling With ALMA
arxiv-2211-16732.creator: Anneliese M. Rilinger, Catherine C. Espaillat, Zihua Xin, Álvaro Ribas, Enrique Macías, Sarah Luettgen
arxiv-2211-16732.description: Abstract We present spectral energy distribution (SED) modeling of 338 disks around T Tauri stars from eleven star-forming regions, ranging from ∼ \sim 0.5 to 10 Myr old. The disk masses we infer from our SED models are typically greater than those reported from (sub)mm surveys by a factor of 1.

arxiv-2212-01784.title: On the Analysis of a Multipartite Entanglement Distribution Switch DOI: 10.1145/3393691.3394203 ISBN: 978-1-4503-7985-4/20/06 CCS: Networks Network performance evaluation CCS: Hardware Quantum communication and cryptography
arxiv-2212-01784.creator: Philippe Nain, Gayane Vardoyan, Saikat Guha, Don Towsley
arxiv-2212-01784.description: Abstract . We study a quantum switch that distributes maximally entangled multipartite states to sets of users. The entanglement switching process requires two steps: first, each user attempts to generate bipartite entanglement between itself and the switch; and second, the switch performs local operations and a measurement to create multipartite entanglement for a set of users.

arxiv-2310-11944.title: Output Corridor Control via Design of Impulsive Goodwin’s Oscillator
arxiv-2310-11944.creator: Alexander Medvedev, Anton V. Proskurnikov, Zhanybai T. Zhusubaliyev
arxiv-2310-11944.description: Abstract In the Impulsive Goodwin’s oscillator (IGO), a continuous positive linear time-invariant (LTI) plant is controlled by an amplitude- and frequency-modulated feedback into an oscillating solution. Self-sustained oscillations in the IGO model have been extensively used to portray periodic rhythms in endocrine systems, whereas the potential of the concept as a controller design approach still remains mainly unexplored.

arxiv-2401-15105.title: Diffusion Enhancement for Cloud Removal in Ultra-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery Thanks: This work was supported in part by the Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of Future Networks of Intelligence under Grant 2022B1212010001, and the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant 42371
arxiv-2401-15105.creator: Jialu Sui, Yiyang Ma, Wenhan Yang, Xiaokang Zhang
arxiv-2401-15105.description: Abstract The presence of cloud layers severely compromises the quality and effectiveness of optical remote sensing (RS) images. However, existing deep-learning (DL)-based Cloud Removal (CR) techniques encounter difficulties in accurately reconstructing the original visual authenticity and detailed semantic content of the images. To tackle this challenge, this work proposes to encompass enhancements at the data and methodology fronts.

arxiv-2404-11359.creator: E. Filandri, L. Girlanda, A. Kievsky, L.E. Marcucci, M. Viviani

arxiv-2510-08650.title: QuIRK : Quantum-Inspired Re-uploading KAN
arxiv-2510-08650.creator: Vinayak Sharma, Ashish Padhy, Lord Sen, Vijay Jagdish Karanjkar, Sourav Behera, Shyamapada Mukherjee, Aviral Shrivastava
arxiv-2510-08650.description: Abstract Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks or KANs have shown the ability to outperform classical Deep Neural Networks, while using far fewer trainable parameters for regression problems on scientific domains. Even more powerful has been their interpretability due to their structure being composed of univariate B-Spline functions. This enables us to derive closed-form equations from trained KANs for a wide range of problems.

arxiv-2510-15106.title: PoTS: Proof-of-Training-Steps for Backdoor Detection in Large Language Models
arxiv-2510-15106.creator: Issam Seddik, Sami Souihi, Mohamed Tamaazousti, Sara Tucci Piergiovanni
arxiv-2510-15106.description: Abstract As Large Language Models (LLMs) gain traction across critical domains, ensuring secure and trustworthy training processes has become a major concern. Backdoor attacks, among various threats—where malicious actors inject hidden triggers into training data—are particularly insidious and difficult to detect.

pmc-10603044.title: Low-dose ethanol consumption inhibits neutrophil extracellular traps formation to alleviate rheumatoid arthritis
pmc-10603044.creator: Lin Jin, Ziwei Zhang, Pin Pan, Yuchen Zhao, Mengqi Zhou, Lianghu Liu, Yuanfang Zhai, Han Wang, Li Xu, Dan Mei, Han Zhang, Yining Yang, Jinghan Hua, Xianzheng Zhang, Lingling Zhang
pmc-10603044.description: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease. Ethanol consumption has been reported to reduce morbidity in RA patients, but the mechanism behind it remains unclear. Our results showed that Muribaculaceae was predominant in the gut microbiota of mice after ethanol treatment, and the levels of microbiota metabolite acetate were increased.

pmc-10735561.title: INTERDISCIPLINARY PERSPECTIVES ON THE INTERSECTION OF CANCER AND COGNITIVE DECLINE
pmc-10735561.creator: Judith Carroll, Lauren Stratton, Brent Small
pmc-10735561.description: The population of older cancer survivors in the United States is rapidly growing. The long-term cognitive aging of older cancer survivors is not well understood, as large-scale epidemiological studies often show a paradoxical inverse association between cancer history and subsequent dementia; yet cancer survivors often experience cognitive impairment symptoms in the short-term following treatment.

pmc-11450094.title: TRIB3 inhibition by palbociclib sensitizes prostate cancer to ferroptosis via downregulating SOX2/SLC7A11 expression
pmc-11450094.creator: Yangyi Zhang, Chenyu Liu, Yalan Yang, He Ren, Tianyi Ren, Yinuo Huang, Shinan Zhang, Qiang Sun, Hongyan Huang
pmc-11450094.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Palbociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor approved for the treatment of breast cancer by suppressing cell proliferation. However, monotherapy with palbociclib was discouraging in prostate cancer, calling for a mechanism-based effective therapy. In this study, we reported in prostate cancer that palbociclib is a potent sensitizer of ferroptosis, which is worked out by downregulating the expression of TRIB3, a gene highly expressed in prostate cancer.

pmc-11488284.title: Antibody-targeted T cells and natural killer cells for cancer immunotherapy
pmc-11488284.creator: Ashley R Sutherland, Brijesh Parlekar, David W Livingstone, Andrés X Medina, Wendy Bernhard, Tays Hernández García, John DeCoteau, C Ronald Geyer
pmc-11488284.description: BackgroundAdoptive cell cancer therapies aim to re-engineer a patient’s immune cells to mount an anti-cancer response. Chimeric antigen receptor T and natural killer cells have been engineered and proved successful in treating some cancers; however, the genetic methods for engineering are laborious, expensive, and inefficient and can cause severe toxicities when they over-proliferate.

pmc-11692443.title: CARE NEEDS AND LIFE SATISFACTION IN FRAIL OLDER ADULTS: THE MODERATING EFFECT OF AGE-FRIENDLY ENVIRONMENTS
pmc-11692443.creator: Inhye Jung, Miseon Kang, Seolah Lee, Hyo Jung Lee
pmc-11692443.description: Frail older adults often face challenges in performing Activities of Daily Living (ADL) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL), leading to diminished quality of life. Age-friendly environments, designed to facilitate aging in place, aim to enhance the well-being of older adults and their family members of all ages by modifying their surroundings and promoting adaptation.

pmc-11905936.title: A Glycolysis and gluconeogenesis-related model for breast cancer prognosis
pmc-11905936.creator: Penglu Yang, Xiong Jiao
pmc-11905936.description: BackgroundBreast cancer is a malignant tumor with high morbidity and mortality, which seriously endangers the health of women around the world. Biomarker-based exploration will be effective for better diagnosis, prediction and targeted therapy.ObjectiveTo construct biomarker models related to glycolysis and gluconeogenesis in breast cancer.

pmc-13145000.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1547 RISK FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH PATIENT REPORTED EXPERIENCE MEASURES AMONG PATIENTS WITH STROKE IN ARMENIA
pmc-13145000.creator: Lilit Avetisyan, Yeva Sahakyan, Lusine Abrahamyan
pmc-13145000.description: Background and aimsPatient-reported experience measures provide insight into perceived quality of care. This study explored risk factors associated with overall hospital rating among hospitalized stroke patients.MethodsStroke patients treated in a tertiary hospital (Sep 2020- Feb 2021) were surveyed via phone using an adapted HCAHPS questionnaire.

pmc-13435570.title: Predicting emotional valence in autism: a preregistered study in the Bayesian Brain framework
pmc-13435570.creator: Irene Sophia Plank, Alexandra Pior, Anna Yurova, Julia Nowak, Zhuanghua Shi, Christine M. Falter-Wagner
pmc-13435570.description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) affects social interaction, communication and behavioural flexibility. Recent theories grounded in the Bayesian Brain Framework propose that autistic individuals process environmental uncertainty differently, overweighting volatility when updating predictions about the world. However, the robustness of these predictive processing differences and their relevance to core symptoms remains unclear.

uslaw-usc-t15-s7421.title: 15 U.S.C. § 7421 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t15-s7421.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t15-s7421.description: United States Code, Title 15 (Commerce And Trade); Chapter 100A (Cybersecurity Enhancement). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In this chapter: (1) Cybersecurity mission The term “cybersecurity mission” means activities that encompass the full range of threat reduction, vulnerability reduction, deterrence, international engagement, incident response, resiliency, and recovery policies and activities, including computer network operations, information assurance, law enforcement, diplomacy, military, and intelligence.
